task: Redesign the Restaurant minigame in esl-likes into a working-memory service game: adopt the shared speech-focus service clock, replace the difficulty ladder (never one customer), add the raised-hand order cue, add wrong-delivery friction, add a first-try combo, make each customer's food independent with repeats allowed, extract the scoring into a pure tested module, and add a debug hook plus an updated scripted playthrough.
notes: READ FIRST, in this order: SPEC.md section 3 subsection 'Protected speech focus', SPEC.md section 4 (the whole Restaurant section — it was rewritten today and is the frozen design you are implementing, including 'Identity', 'Wrong delivery', 'Each customer's food is independent', and 'Difficulty'), then the four 2026-09-12 entries at the end of DESIGN_DECISIONS.md. Those documents are the contract. Where this brief and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins and you should say so in your summary.

CONTEXT. esl-likes is a 3D ESL game for Japanese Grade 3 children on classroom Chromebooks. The child speaks English to NPCs: they ask 'What food do you like?' and the NPC answers 'I like curry.' The frozen rules are that the NPC's answer must be information the child genuinely needs, and that recognition noise is the game's problem and never the child's.

WHY THE REDESIGN. Today level 1 seats exactly ONE customer, so the only ready dish obviously belongs to them and the English answer is unnecessary — the anti-shortcut rule fails at the easiest level, where it matters most. Restaurant must become the working-memory stage whose real question is 'curry is ready, WHO said curry?'. Drink Stand (a separate order, running in parallel) owns the other question, 'where is the milk machine?'. Do not make Restaurant more like Drink Stand.

ALREADY DONE FOR YOU — do not rebuild or modify these. (1) src/systems/speechFocus.js exists, is tested and is frozen: `createSpeechFocus({ floor = 0, enterDuration = 0.12, releaseDuration = 0.35 })` returns `{ begin(reason), end(), cancel(), update(dt), serviceDelta(dt), get active, get scale }`. scale is 1 in normal play, ramps to the floor while focused, and ramps back to exactly 1 after end(). begin() is idempotent; cancel() snaps back to 1 for minigame exit. (2) All new Japanese UI strings already exist in src/config/lesson.js under UI.restaurant: `stepAway`, `wantsToOrder`, `orderTaken`, `combo` ('{count} コンボ！', use with the existing formatUi helper), and `wrongDish` which is now just 'ちがうみたい…'. Use these; do NOT edit src/config/lesson.js, because a parallel order is forbidden from touching it too and any edit there will conflict.

THE SERVICE CLOCK — the central change, do this first. Restaurant currently drives everything from `elapsed`, which accumulates raw frame dt. Introduce a separate service clock: keep `elapsed` for cosmetic animation (steam drift, bell pulse, meter billboarding) and add `serviceElapsed` advanced by `focus.serviceDelta(safeDt)`. EVERY pressure clock must read the service delta or serviceElapsed, never raw dt: customer spawn scheduling, patience drain, kitchen preparation countdown, the carried dish's cooling (`carrySeconds`), and the new refusal locks. Call `focus.update(safeDt)` once per frame with the real dt. The point of this structure is that a future timer added to this file freezes correctly by default instead of needing to remember a guard. Do not write per-timer `if (questionCustomer !== customer)` guards — that pattern is what the redesign removes.

FOCUS LIFECYCLE. Call `focus.begin()` when the talk prompt is opened for a customer (today: targetQuestion) and `focus.end()` when it resolves or is abandoned (today: acceptQuestion, and clearQuestion when the child walks away). Focus must therefore cover the whole interaction: holding the button, recognition running, the pause while it is judged, a RETRY after a failed recognition, and the mic-free read-and-tap fallback. The acceptance test is that a sentence needing two attempts costs no more service time than one that worked first try. Also call `focus.begin()` for the final turnaround prompt, and `focus.cancel()` in exit(). An optional cheap polish: duck the ambient/service audio while focused. Do NOT move the camera during focus and do NOT add postprocessing — camera re-framing caused a real bug in this project before, and there is no budget for effects on a classroom Chromebook.

DIFFICULTY — replace the DIFFICULTY table. L1: 3 customers seated, at most ONE order active (taken but not yet delivered) at a time, at most one ready dish at a time, very generous patience. L2: 4 customers, 2-3 orders active. L3: 5 customers, 3-4 orders active. The existing TABLES array already has 5 entries; CUSTOMER_TINTS and the model list `['e','f','i','m']` only have 4, so extend both to 5 with a visually distinct fifth customer. Customers must be visually distinguishable from each other at a glance. 'At most N active orders' is what creates the Easy experience: three people are seated and could each have asked, but only one order is in flight, so the child holds one person-food pair at a time while still needing the answer to place it.

ORDER GATING AND THE RAISED-HAND CUE. Customers no longer simply spawn on a timer into a askable state. A seated customer becomes ready-to-order only when the active-order budget allows, and while ready-to-order they show a clear non-food cue — a raised hand, or a ❓ billboard above them, reusing the existing billboarding approach used for patience meters. The cue means 'somebody wants to order'; it must NEVER hint at what they want. It clears the instant the order is taken. Use UI.restaurant.wantsToOrder for the instruction line and orderTaken on acceptance. This cue is required for readability: at five customers a child cannot otherwise tell who is waiting.

PATIENCE. A customer who has NOT yet ordered loses no patience at all on L1, and loses it slowly on L2/L3. Pressure becomes real only after their order has been taken. This mirrors the Drink Stand rule that a queued customer has no countdown. Patience never creates a fail state; a customer who runs out waves and leaves and the round continues.

FOOD ASSIGNMENT — a real anti-shortcut fix. Today `const menu = shuffled(LESSON.answers); const food = menu[index % menu.length];` deals five distinct foods to up to five customers, so at L3 every food appears exactly once and the last order is deducible by elimination. Choose each customer's food independently and uniformly at random instead, repeats allowed, nothing removed from the pool. THEN, because two identical plates must not create an unfair delivery, change delivery matching from plate identity to FOOD identity: a ready dish satisfies any customer who ordered that food and is still awaiting it. If two customers ordered curry and two curries are ready, either curry satisfies either of them. Today `deliver()` compares `carried !== customer`; that must become a food comparison plus an awaiting check. See the SPEC subsection and the DESIGN_DECISIONS entry for the rationale.

WRONG DELIVERY — the friction, and read this carefully because the obvious implementation is the one that was rejected. On a wrong delivery: the customer politely refuses in Japanese (UI.restaurant.wrongDish), the English answer is NOT repeated, no hint about the food appears, the dish STAYS IN THE PLAYER'S HANDS, and that order loses its first-try credit and resets the combo. Then a short per-customer refusal lock (about 5 seconds of service time) during which that customer will not reconsider, AND the player must leave that customer's interaction radius before offering the dish to anybody else — so the brute-force sweep A→wrong→B→wrong→C→correct costs real time while a child who listened delivers immediately. Show UI.restaurant.stepAway. Explicitly REJECTED, do not implement: making the player carry a refused dish back to the pickup counter. That turns a listening mistake into a temperature penalty plus a long walk and punishes the least confident child hardest. Nothing is ever permanently failed; the order stays recoverable.

COMBO. Add a visible combo for consecutive FIRST-TRY correct deliveries, shown as UI.restaurant.combo ('2 コンボ！'), styled like the existing Drink Stand combo pop (see src/minigames/drinkStand/index.js for the CSS pattern and reuse the look, but keep it local to this file — do not extract a shared component). It increments only on a first-attempt correct delivery and resets on a wrong delivery. It must NOT be tied to speaking speed, recognition latency or pronunciation in any way. Using 🔊 Listen Again forfeits that customer's memory bonus but does NOT break the delivery combo — keep those two concepts separate.

KEEP ALL OF THIS WORKING: the room, tables, kitchen counter, bell, the dish meshes and steam, the hot/warm/cold temperature system (cold food is still accepted and never fails), the patience meters, movement and collision, the click/tap-to-walk route if present, the dialogue bubbles, 🔊 もういちど きく (listening support, never failure, forfeits only the memory bonus), the final turnaround where the host asks the child and any valid food answer is accepted, the settings subscription, the finish() payload shape `{ stars, detail: { category, answer } }`, and full disposal in exit() including the new customers, cue meshes and the focus cancel. Preparation time must stay a property of the dish (FOOD_PREP_SECONDS) so readiness order stays independent of asking order, and the ready dish must keep going to a randomly chosen free counter slot.

EXTRACT THE SCORING. Create src/minigames/restaurant/scoring.js as a pure module with no DOM and no three.js, mirroring the house style of src/minigames/drinkStand/scoring.js, and move the star calculation there. It should score from per-customer records (delivered or left, first-try or not, temperature score, patience at delivery, whether Listen Again was used) and return at least `{ earned, maximum, ratio, stars, firstTryCount, firstTryShare }`. Keep the existing spirit: correct delivery dominates, temperature and remaining patience add a little, the memory bonus is small, and a low first-try share should cap the result below three stars. Add src/minigames/restaurant/scoring.test.mjs (node:test + node:assert/strict) covering: a perfect first-try session reaching three stars, a session of correct-but-second-attempt deliveries scoring lower, Listen Again costing only the memory bonus and never normal credit, cold food still earning credit, a customer who left earning nothing, and the first-try cap. Also unit-test the pure parts of the new rules wherever you can reach them without a DOM — food choice allowing repeats, and the refusal-lock timing logic — extracting a tiny pure helper if that is what makes them testable. Do not try to unit-test three.js scene code.

DEBUG HOOK AND PLAYTHROUGH. Restaurant has no debug hook, which is why its scripted playthrough cannot drive the new mechanics. Add one exactly like the Drink Stand's: install `window.__eslDebug.restaurant` as a getter returning a snapshot, and remove it in exit() with the same root-cleanup logic (see installDebugHook / removeDebugHook / debugSnapshot / projectObject in src/minigames/drinkStand/index.js and copy that approach). The snapshot must expose enough to drive and assert a playthrough: phase, level, per-customer index/state/food/whether the order cue is showing/screen position of the click target, the ready dishes with their food and counter slot and screen position, what is carried, the combo, and whether focus is active. Then update scripts/playthrough.mjs — the existing Restaurant playthrough — to the new mechanics, following the structure of scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs: a listening session that asks, remembers and delivers correctly and expects three stars, and an anti-shortcut session that ignores the answers and sweeps customers, which must NOT reach three stars. Add a check that a wrong delivery leaves the dish in hand and does not repeat the English, and a check that all patience is frozen while a prompt is open.

BEHAVIOURAL ACCEPTANCE IS REQUIRED — this is gameplay and visual work, so passing tests are not evidence that it plays correctly. Run the real thing and look at it: `npm run build`, serve it with `npx vite preview --port 5199`, and run your updated playthrough against it at viewport 1366x768, which is the real classroom Chromebook resolution. Capture screenshots of: the room with all customers seated and at least one raised-hand cue visible, a moment with two ready dishes on the counter, a carried dish, a wrong-delivery refusal, the combo pop, and the turnaround. Report what you actually observed on the result's `behavioralValidation` field with `performed`, `observed: true` ONLY if you really looked at rendered output, `method`, `viewport: '1366x768'`, `checks` and `passed`. Saying it looks right without having looked is a claim, not an observation, and will be treated as such. Specifically confirm by looking: customers are distinguishable, the raised-hand cue is noticeable and not food-related, ready dishes are recognisable as their food, patience meters do not clutter the scene, and nothing clips through tables.

If your own new Playwright checks fail, remember the harness is new and therefore untrusted: verify the locator, viewport and scene state before concluding the game is broken. Inspect the screenshot or DOM first.

Append a short DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entry ONLY if you make a design decision this brief and SPEC do not already cover. The four entries for today's redesign are already written — do not duplicate or rewrite them, and do not edit SPEC.md.
requirements: A separate service clock drives every pressure timer (spawning, patience, kitchen preparation, carried-dish cooling, refusal locks) via focus.serviceDelta, while cosmetic animation keeps using raw frame dt; focus.update runs once per frame and focus.cancel runs in exit

While a talk prompt is open — including a retry after failed recognition and the mic-free fallback route — no customer's patience drains, no dish cooks, no dish cools, and no customer spawns or becomes ready to order
Difficulty is 3 customers with 1 active order, 4 with 2-3, and 5 with 3-4; level 1 never has fewer than 3 seated customers, and there are 5 visually distinct customer appearances available
A customer ready to order shows a clear cue that carries no information about which food they want, and the cue clears when the order is taken
A customer who has not yet ordered loses no patience on level 1 and loses it slowly above; patience never produces a fail state

Each customer's food is chosen independently and uniformly with repeats allowed, and a ready dish is matched to a customer by food rather than by plate identity, so either of two identical dishes satisfies either customer who ordered it

A wrong delivery refuses politely in Japanese, does not repeat the English answer, gives no food hint, leaves the dish in the player's hands, resets the combo, loses first-try credit, and applies both a short per-customer refusal lock and a requirement to leave that customer's radius before trying another — and the dish is never permanently lost
A refused dish is never required to be returned to the pickup counter
A visible combo counts consecutive first-try correct deliveries, resets on a wrong delivery, and is independent of speaking speed, recognition latency and Listen Again
Kitchen preparation time still depends on the food and the ready dish still appears at a randomly chosen free counter slot, so readiness order is independent of asking order

src/minigames/restaurant/scoring.js is a pure module with no DOM or three.js dependency, and src/minigames/restaurant/scoring.test.mjs covers perfect first-try play, second-attempt play, Listen Again costing only the memory bonus, cold food still earning credit, a customer who left, and the first-try cap

window.__eslDebug.restaurant exposes phase, level, per-customer state including food and cue and screen position, ready dishes with food and slot, the carried dish, the combo and whether focus is active; and it is removed cleanly in exit

scripts/playthrough.mjs is updated to the new mechanics with a listening session reaching three stars and an anti-shortcut sweep session that does not, plus checks that a wrong delivery keeps the dish and does not repeat the English, and that patience is frozen during a prompt
The existing room, dishes, temperature system, movement, dialogue, Listen Again, turnaround, settings subscription, finish payload shape and full resource disposal all still work
npm test passes including the pre-existing 139 tests, npm run build is clean, and the Restaurant playthrough passes at 1366x768

behavioralValidation is reported from rendered output actually observed, with screenshots covering the seated room with an order cue, two ready dishes, a carried dish, a wrong-delivery refusal, the combo and the turnaround

Do NOT modify src/systems/speechFocus.js or its test — that module is frozen and already reviewed
Do NOT modify src/minigames/drinkStand/** — a parallel order owns those files right now. Read them for patterns, never edit them
Do NOT modify SPEC.md, and do not rewrite the existing 2026-09-12 DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entries

Do not modify the other minigames (coloring, sports, zoo) or the shared shell, HUD, dialogue, speech matcher, characters, progression or save systems; if you believe a shared file must change, stop and report instead
Do not implement a two-dish tray or any multi-carry mechanic — it is explicitly deferred
Do not move the camera during speech focus, add postprocessing, add large particle systems, add per-frame allocations in the update loop, or add any npm dependency
Do not extract a shared service-game abstraction between Restaurant and Drink Stand; they are deliberately different controllers
Edit files with your structured patch/edit tool. If a shell-based edit fails once because of quoting or escaping, switch to the structured mechanism — do not try another escaped variant
